title: Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B on iac-bench 2026-11
summary: How Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 81.6, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.
body_markdown:

## Summary


Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B places eleventh of 16 by composite (81.6), between GLM-5.3 (82.5) and GPT-6 Luna (81.5), with a 95% rank interval of 7–13. Against its neighbours the bootstrap is close to a coin flip: it finishes ahead of Kimi K3 in 48% of resamples, GPT-6 Luna in 45% and GLM-5.3 in 43%, and ahead of Kimi K3.1 Pro in 2%. All 9 attempts cost $4.40, against $3.52 for Kimi K3.1 Pro, $3.96 for Kimi K3, $8.46 for GLM-5.3 and $0.88 for DeepSeek V4 Pro.


All 9 attempts planned. 4 of 9 carry a security finding: one on S3 and three on App Service. Cloud SQL (G002) is its strongest fixture, fifth in the field by median composite (89.0) and the highest of the open-weight models. App Service (G003) is its weakest, thirteenth (71.7).

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **Cloud SQL posture fixed in code (3/3).**` ipv4_enabled = false` and` ssl_mode = "ENCRYPTED_ONLY"` are literals, where Kimi K3 lets` ssl_mode` be weakened in 3/3. The private network is derived from` environment` (` apps-<environment>` ).
- **Identity-only database access.** IAM database login (E3), declared users (E5) and workload identities (E7) in 3/3, with no password users. One attempt merges` cloudsql.iam_authentication` ,` log_connections` and` log_disconnections` over the DBA's flags, rejects any input that sets them, and refuses to disable deletion protection in` prod` .
- **S3 expertise.** 6 of 7 expertise items in 3/3, including bucket-owner-enforced ownership (E1), a TLS-deny policy (E4) and ready-to-attach consumer policies (E9). S3 judge median 94.7.
- **Every module plans (9/9),** where Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 each fail one App Service attempt. Autoscale rules (E1), the container port (E2) and a staging slot (` H9` ) appear in 3/3.


## Weaknesses


- **Security findings:**` H1` on S3 (e1); on App Service` H2` (e1),` H1` and` H2` (e2),` H1` (e3). Kimi K3.1 Pro has none. The cause is under *Characteristic patterns* .
- **Documentation that contradicts the code** ( *Documentation* 0 in 5 of 9 attempts; only DeepSeek V4 Pro has more, 6/9):


- every App Service README describes deploying a new image to the staging slot and then swapping, but one image input feeds both the production app and the slot (3/3);
- Cloud SQL descriptions ask for full service-account emails, which become` google_sql_user` names that PostgreSQL rejects until the` .gserviceaccount.com` suffix is trimmed (3/3). The judge caught it; the rubric did not.


- **Large App Service interfaces:** 27, 29 and 41 inputs against a budget of 20 (` A7` partial or zero, 3/3). The 41-input attempt also exposes` http2_enabled` (` A6` ).
- **Gaps on S3 and Cloud SQL:**


- no bucket policy admits the logging service (` H13` , 3/3); logging (` H9` ) and a provider block with a region input (` H15` ) each appear in 1/3;
- backups and point-in-time recovery cannot be turned off (` H4` /` H5` at 0.75, 3/3), and backups never outlive the instance (E1, 0/3);
- no` deletion_policy` in either attempt that declares databases (` H11` ).


- **Provider constraints that admit a new major** in 5 of 9 attempts (` B1` ):` >= 5.0` or` >= 6.0` on S3 (3/3), and` >= 5.30.0, < 7.0.0` spanning two majors on Cloud SQL (2/3).


## Characteristic patterns


-


**Wide spread within a fixture.** Mechanical scores run 0.57–0.87 on S3 and 0.53–0.80 on App Service, against a spread of 0.05 on Cloud SQL, all from modules that plan. Each sample hardcodes a different subset of the security posture and exposes the rest:


- S3 e1 adds` allow_public_access` , which turns off all four public-access-block settings (` H1` , 18 of 86 rubric weight). The other two S3 attempts keep them fixed;
- App Service e1 hardcodes HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 and FTP off, but never sets the basic-auth publishing flags, which default to on (` H2` );
- e3 turns basic auth off and hardcodes TLS 1.2, then exposes` https_only` and the managed identity as inputs (` H1` ,` H4` ; excerpt below);
- e2 sets neither basic-auth flag, leaves` https_only` off the slot, and exposes` minimum_tls_version` and` ftps_state` with validations that accept` "1.0"` and` "AllAllowed"` (` H1` ,` H2` ,` H3` ).


Kimi K3.1 Pro varies by at most 0.075 on any fixture. Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 have wider App Service spreads, but theirs come from a failed plan.


-


**Long transcripts.** Median 37,210 output tokens per attempt, second in the field after GLM-5.3. The longest (App Service e2: 68,729 tokens, $1.02, 41 inputs) is also its lowest-scoring attempt (59.4).


## Representative excerpt


` G003/qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b-e3/main.tf` lines 48–67


```text
https_only                    = var.https_only
public_network_access_enabled = var.public_network_access_enabled
virtual_network_subnet_id     = var.virtual_network_subnet_id


# HTTP APIs are stateless; session affinity only pins users to instances
# that may be recycled, so keep it off.
client_affinity_enabled = false


# Images arrive from a container registry, never over password-based
# publishing endpoints.
ftp_publish_basic_authentication_enabled       = false
webdeploy_publish_basic_authentication_enabled = false


dynamic "identity" {
for_each = var.managed_identity_enabled ? ["SystemAssigned"] : []


content {
type = identity.value
}
}


```


One App Service resource, two postures. Basic-auth publishing is hardcoded off with a comment explaining why, while HTTPS-only and the managed identity are left to inputs (` https_only` ,` managed_identity_enabled` ). Both default to the secure setting, but either can be switched off, which costs this attempt` H1` and` H4` . Each App Service sample draws this line in a different place.
